items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I got in hassles with Wexler, I got in hassles with Ahmet... Ahmet got involved... Ahmet and I were never right after that.

ctx.x: And did you go to those?

Oh are you kidding? I lived in those places. First of all, because I was on the air I could go to any club I wanted to and I didn’t have to pay, you know and that was a big deal then even though it was two dollars on the door — you know when Miles came to town it was three. It was like that. But I was also plotting and scheming. I mean I was a disc jockey, and I always wanted to be a disc jockey, but I always wanted to be a record producer. So I would go in there and I would, aside from getting all the records…

producer, I think I annoyed myself into a job. I produced some stuff independently that they put out, but that’s where I wanted to work was Atlantic Records. And what was your question because I’m leading towards something and now I got lost in my own nonsense.
